title: Shortcuts: a table shortcut, a folder shortcut, and a chain to avoid
objective_text: Fix three shortcuts in a lakehouse: where each goes, what it points at, what it's called and how it signs in, so tables show up as tables and files as files.
scenario: SalesLH needs CRM customers, a partner's CSV exports and last year's archived orders without copying any of them. Someone created three shortcuts, and none of them works as intended: two tables don't appear, and the partner folder fails to open.
engine_label: A model of a lakehouse's shortcuts, checked on this PC
verifies: Your shortcuts sit where OneLake allows them, use names a table can have, point straight at their sources and use the right sign-in, as the shortcuts page describes it, checked against a model on this PC.
does_not_verify: That the shortcuts resolve in Fabric: nothing is created here.
Schema shortcuts in schema-enabled lakehouses, shortcut caching, and other sources such as S3 or Dataverse.
Whether the callers have permission on the target lakehouses.

expected.description: customers in Tables to CRM_LH/Tables/customers with caller identity; partner in Files to the ADLS container with a connection; orders_2025 in Tables, no spaces.

validation.fail: A table shortcut won't show up as a table.
validation.pass: Both table shortcuts sit at the top of Tables with names Delta accepts.

rules.why: In Tables, shortcuts can only be created at the top level, not in subfolders.

validation.fail: The customers shortcut goes through another shortcut.
validation.pass: customers points straight at CRM_LH's table.

rules.why: A shortcut to a shortcut breaks when the middle one moves, and a path has a limit on how many shortcuts it can pass through. Point at the source.

validation.fail: The partner files aren't set up as files from an external source.
validation.pass: The partner files are a Files shortcut that signs in with its connection.

rules.why: CSV files aren't a Delta table; in Files a shortcut can go at any level.
ADLS and S3 shortcuts use the cloud connection's credential; OneLake shortcuts use the caller's identity.

hints: Where in Tables can a shortcut go? Where in Files?
What happens to a table name with a space in Delta?
Should a shortcut point at another shortcut, or at the source?
Which shortcuts use the caller's identity, and which use a connection?
explanation: A shortcut in Tables must be at the top level, and its target must be in a table format such as Delta for the lakehouse to recognize it as a table; a name with a space isn't recognized. Files shortcuts can go at any level and suit non-table data such as CSV. Pointing at another shortcut builds a chain that breaks when a link moves and counts against the limit of shortcuts in one path, so point at the source. OneLake shortcuts use the caller's identity; ADLS and S3 shortcuts use a cloud connection. Deleting a shortcut never deletes its target.
review_notes: Checked on Learn 2026-11-06 (onelake-shortcuts): Tables shortcuts only at the top level, Files at any level; a Delta target is recognized as a table; names with spaces aren't; a path supports up to 10 shortcuts; OneLake shortcuts use the caller's identity, ADLS and S3 use cloud connections; deleting a shortcut leaves the target.
